newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS - Malaysia stocks rebound, could ease again.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Malaysia stocks rebound, could ease again.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares closed higher on Wednesday on a technical rebound after two days of sharp falls, dealers and analysts said.
The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index closed 1.29 percent, or 11.58 points, higher at 908.83. It had peaked at 919.58.
The index has lost 23.53 points, or 2.5 percent, since last Friday. The index has lost more than 25 percent this year.
"It is very much a technical rebound," said a senior foreign fund manager in Kaula Lumpur.

Dealers and analysts said local and foreign institutional investors had been seen selectively buying large-capitalised issues such as Telekom and Maybank. the stocks gaines 10 cents and 50 cents respectively.
Power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd were also actively traded, gaining 15 cents and 10 cents respectively.
The four stocks together have a 44 percent weightage on the Composite Index.
"There has been some local (institutional) buying. There has been some nibbling by foreigners, but they are still net sellers," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.
"The rebound is not that great when you consider that the index has fallen (so sharply) over the last few days," said Faez Khairuddin, head of research at SJ Securities.

Some dealers and analysts attributed the rebound to statements by Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Tuesday that the government may defer some large infrastructure projects to reduce the country's current account deficit.
He was responding to fears expressed by economists that Malaysia's economy may be overheating.
But earlier comments by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad indicating that he would continue to pursue a high-growth economic policy, were seen as contradictory to Anwar's statements, said analysts.
"They have to stop contradicting each other. If nothing is done I see the market going down further," said a senior foreign fund manager in Kuala Lumpur.
"Everything is a moving target at the moment. There have been conflicting statements about important matters which have affected the confidence of local and foreign investors," he said.
Underlying concerns over the direction of the ringgit's value continued to be a mitigating factor against any definitive rebound.
"This is a short-term rebound. I'm inclined to believe it is not sustainable. We are not quite out of the woods yet; there are still concerns over the ringgit," said Faez.
Anwar said on Tuesday Malaysia would not defend the ringgit against speculative attacks. The ringgit has eased over 11 percent in the last month.
The ringgit remains under pressure, trading in a range of 2.7650 and 2.7950 to a dollar.
